intro: I believe learning and teaching work best when five conditions are in place. The explanations below draw on my full teaching philosophy.

values.title: Cultivating curiosity and interest
values.text: I want a classroom where curiosity leads and intellectual challenge sparks interest in learning. I open inquiries with provocations that draw students in and show me what they already know.

values.title: Activating and honoring thinking
values.text: I teach for conceptual understanding, so students treat new knowledge as a springboard for critical thinking. Visible Thinking Routines give that thinking a structure, and they make it something we can discuss, question, and build on.

values.title: Connecting learning within and beyond the content
values.text: Understanding matters when students can apply it to situations they have not met before. I connect units to concepts, to real contexts, and to places beyond the classroom so that learning transfers.

values.title: Developing competencies
values.text: The IB's Approaches to Learning skills (thinking, communication, research, and self-management) sit at the center of my planning. Students practice them repeatedly and reflect on their growth, which builds independent learners and problem-solvers.

values.title: Building trust and relationships
values.text: I use positive discipline and restorative practices, and I treat trusting relationships as the foundation of learning. Respect and empathy make the classroom safe enough for students to take risks and learn from mistakes, and I work to build the same culture among colleagues.
